packages.name: blyxtorch
packages.title: BlyxTorch
packages.description: Train dense networks with SGD or Adam, inspect parameter gradients, and generate standalone Blyx models for regression or classification.
packages.contract: BlyxTorch 0.2.0 uses fixed-shape float64 networks on CPU. Each layer width is 1–64. A model supports up to eight affine layers and 1,024 trainable parameters. The prebuilt 2–4–1 classifier runs immediately. Generating a new executable requires Blyx 0.2.1, Rust and a host linker on the build machine.
api: bt_dual(value, tangent), bt_square(v)
Differentiate a scalar expression in the portable library. The result holds its value and directional derivative.
bt_add, bt_sub, bt_mul, bt_div, bt_relu, bt_tanh, bt_sigmoid
Compose differentiable operations on dual numbers.
bt_init(seed), bt_predict(weights, features)
Initialize and run a generated model module.
bt_sample_loss(weights, features, target), bt_loss_grad(weights, features, target)
Return a loss or a loss followed by every parameter gradient.
blyxtorch emit WIDTHS OBJECTIVE ACTIVATION
Generate a complete Blyx model and CLI. Use mse, binary or softmax with tanh, relu or sigmoid.
train-score TRAIN.csv LABELLED.csv
Train once and report row count and loss on a separate labelled CSV.
train-predict TRAIN.csv FEATURES.csv
Train once and write a probability for each new feature row.
cli: Training writes a checkpoint to standard output. The handbook shows how to save it, predict and inspect gradients on each platform.

projects.title: Calibrate a desk sensor
projects.description: Fit a gain and an offset from five synthetic reference readings using BlyxTorch automatic differentiation. The model predicts 18.625 and 22.375 degrees for two readings held out of training.

projects.title: Predict print-queue waits
projects.description: Classify four new print jobs using a trained two-input network. The starter includes 16 synthetic training rows and six separate evaluation rows. With seed 7, the mean evaluation loss is about 0.00234.

packages.logoAlt: A blue-crested bird with half-lidded eyes and a bright orange bill.

packages.title: LinearFit
packages.description: Train, merge and deploy a single-feature least-squares or ridge regression with an unpenalized intercept.
packages.contract: Provide aligned finite x and y values. At least two rows are required. Set ridge to zero for ordinary least squares, or choose a positive penalty for shrinkage. The centered model keeps predictions stable for features with large offsets.
api: lf_fit(xs, ys, penalty)
Train on a pair of vectors. Returns [mean_x, mean_y, slope].
lf_start(), lf_update(state, x, y), lf_merge(a, b)
Accumulate rows or merge disjoint training batches.
lf_finish(state, penalty), lf_predict(model, x)
Freeze a model and predict a response in the original units.
lf_csv_summary(path)
Import the native csvfit module to read a CSV into a summary that lf_merge or lf_finish can use.
cli: The model learns slope 2 and predicts 11. Add --ridge 5 to shrink the slope to 1.
packages.logoAlt: An ivory gannet dives along the line of its long blue-grey bill.

packages.title: Conformal
packages.description: Calibrate a regression interval from held-out errors and measure coverage on a separate test set.
packages.contract: Use examples held out from model training. Each interval is prediction ± a finite calibration radius. Coverage is marginal under exchangeability, and can differ by subgroup or after a distribution shift. A 90% request needs at least nine calibration examples for a finite interval.
api: cf_calibrate(actual, predicted, numerator, denominator)
Select an observed absolute residual using the finite-sample adjusted rank.
cf_radius(scores, numerator, denominator)
Calibrate from previously calculated nonnegative scores.
cf_interval(prediction, radius), cf_coverage(actual, predicted, radius)
Return the two endpoints, or measure the fraction of a separate test set covered.
packages.logoAlt: A snowy owl cups its speckled wings around its body.

packages.title: Moments
packages.description: Summarize paired observations as they arrive and merge statistics from independent batches.
packages.contract: The state contains count, two means, two centered sums of squares and a cross-product. Merge disjoint batches only. Empty batches act as the identity. Sample standard deviation needs at least two observations.
api: mom_empty(), mom_update(state, x, y)
Create a state and add one observation.
mom_summary(xs, ys), mom_merge(left, right)
Summarize vectors or combine batches in constant additional state.
mom_sample_sd_y(state)
Read the sample standard deviation of the second variable.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin sliding two sets of paired beads onto a shared counting rail.

packages.title: ResidualWatch
packages.description: Monitor prediction drift by detecting sustained upward or downward changes in errors against a frozen reference period.
packages.contract: Keep rows in time order. The reference residual is actual minus prediction, so a positive alarm means sustained underprediction. A constant reference requires an explicit positive scale floor. Choose thresholds against representative stable data.
api: rw_fit(actual, predicted, min_scale)
Freeze row count, mean residual and sample scale from reference data.
rw_training(), rw_train(state, actual, prediction), rw_freeze(state, min_scale)
Learn the same reference one observation at a time.
rw_monitor(), rw_step(state, reference, actual, prediction, allowance, limit)
Update the detector. The third result is +1, −1 or 0.
cli: Reference residuals have mean 0 and sample deviation 1. The first alert is data row 5. The command exits with code 1.
packages.logoAlt: A blue kingfisher with a ragged crest leans forward to watch.

packages.title: CUSUM
packages.description: Detect persistent shifts in a sequence of standardized observations with a two-sided cumulative sum.
packages.contract: Supply standardized observations in order. The allowance controls how much deviation is ignored. The limit is inclusive. An observation following an alarm starts a fresh episode. Tune both values for the time series you monitor.
api: cs_empty()
Start with zero evidence of an upward or downward shift.
cs_step(state, z, allowance, limit)
Return [upward magnitude, downward magnitude, direction]. Save this state for the next point.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin marking where a cumulative staircase crosses an alarm line.

packages.title: ModelGate
packages.description: Compare two binary classifiers on the same observations and stop a release when mistake costs or Brier score regress.
packages.contract: Use paired labels and probabilities in [0,1]. A missed positive can carry a different cost from a false alarm. The sample has two models at 75% accuracy. With a miss costing five times as much, cost per prediction rises from 0.25 to 1.25.
api: gate_passes(baseline_brier, candidate_brier, baseline_cost, candidate_cost, tolerance)
Apply the gate to validated per-row metrics.
--threshold, --fn-cost, --fp-cost, --brier-tolerance
Configure costs and the maximum increase in mean Brier score.
cli: Returns exit code 1. Both models get three rows right, but the candidate misses the more costly positive.
packages.logoAlt: A grey secretarybird raises a black wing beside its copper eye patch.

packages.title: Classification
packages.description: Measure threshold decisions, false alarms, missed positives and their costs.
packages.contract: Inputs are equal-length vectors of binary labels and finite probabilities. A score equal to the threshold counts as positive. An undefined precision, recall or F1 has value zero.
api: class_confusion(labels, scores, threshold)
Return true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives in that order.
class_precision, class_recall, class_f1
Calculate scalar metrics from the confusion counts.
class_cost(fp, missed, fp_cost, fn_cost)
Compute total weighted cost. Divide by observation count for cost per row.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin sorting prediction shapes into a four-cell confusion matrix.

packages.title: Calibration
packages.description: Check agreement between predicted probabilities and observed outcomes.
packages.contract: Use equal-length, nonempty vectors of 0/1 labels and probabilities. Supply between one and 100 bins. A probability of 1 belongs in the last bin. The bin count matters when comparing expected calibration error.
api: cal_brier(labels, scores)
Compute mean squared probability error.
cal_bin(labels, scores, index, bins)
Return a reliability bin’s count, forecast total and outcome total.
cal_ece(labels, scores, bins)
Summarize bin gaps weighted by observation count.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin adjusting a probability point against a diagonal reference line.

packages.title: Retrieval
packages.description: Score ranked search or RAG results without giving repeated document IDs extra credit.
packages.contract: Use finite, whole, nonnegative document IDs up to the largest exactly representable safe integer. Duplicate hits occupy a rank. Precision includes unfilled positions up to the cutoff. The implementation targets small per-query rankings.
api: retrieval_at_k(ranked, relevant, k)
Return precision, recall, reciprocal rank and average precision at the cutoff.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin lifting a repeated document out of a ranked stack.

packages.title: Backtest
packages.description: Evaluate forecasts in time order with a gap for delayed observations and disjoint test windows.
packages.contract: Choose an initial training history, a positive horizon and a nonnegative gap. A zero training window expands the history. A positive window caps its length. The final incomplete test horizon is omitted.
api: bt_fold_count(n, initial, horizon, gap), bt_fold(n, initial, horizon, gap, window, fold)
Plan training and test windows with zero-based, exclusive end indices.
bt_baselines(series, initial, horizon, gap, window)
Score a last-value and training-mean baseline on identical observations.
bt_score(series, forecasts, initial, horizon, gap)
Calculate mean absolute and signed error of submitted forecasts.
packages.logoAlt: A silver Arctic tern banks back towards its forked tail.

packages.name: blyx-swiftlet
packages.title: Swiftlet
packages.description: Dispatch a method and request path against a table of literal and parameterized routes. Return a matched template and the methods a client can use.
packages.contract: Register a method and an absolute path template separated by one space. GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS use explicit registrations. Literal segments outrank parameters by their count. Equally specific templates use registration order. The matcher strips the query, preserves percent encoding and treats a trailing slash as significant. Hosting, URL decoding and authentication belong to the application.
api: sw_dispatch(routes, method, target)
Import router. Returns status text, matched template, and the Allow value in a three-element argument list.
sw_param(template, target, name)
Extract an encoded path parameter from a matching path. An absent capture returns an empty string.
sw_enable(mask, method), sw_status(found, mask, method)
Build a method set and apply the same status decisions as the router. Start at zero.
sw_allow(mask)
Generate the comma-separated list of registered HTTP methods.

workflow.title: Route a book catalog request
workflow.description: Pass PATCH and /books/42?preview=yes to the dispatcher. It selects /books/:id and extracts 42. Try the same method on /books/new, an explicitly read-only resource. The CGI example also serves a health check through an existing web server.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-swiftlet.git
cd blyx-swiftlet
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A method error and a missing route mean different things to an HTTP client. If their responses share one fallback, clients lose the list of methods a resource accepts. RFC 9110 requires an Allow field on a 405 response.

packages.logoAlt: A dark swiftlet changes direction on long, curved wings.

packages.name: blyx-shrike
packages.title: Shrike
packages.description: Combine lexical and semantic search results by rank, then walk the merged list in a deterministic order.
packages.contract: Supply two ranked vectors of nonnegative integer IDs up to 2^53−1 and an offset from 0 to 1,000,000. The first occurrence in each list contributes 1/(offset + one-based position). Missing IDs contribute zero. Equal scores use ascending ID. Start the cursor at −1. Each next-result call can take quadratic time in the combined shortlist length; use this version with small candidate sets.
api: sh_valid_inputs(left, right, offset)
Validate every ID and the smoothing offset.
sh_score(left, right, id, offset)
Get the fused score of one document. Zero means absent and −1 means invalid input.
sh_next(left, right, offset, previous)
Get the next ID after a cursor, or −1 for exhaustion or invalid input. Each ID is returned once.

workflow.title: Merge two help-center searches
workflow.description: A literal-word search and a paraphrase search return different article IDs. The example prints the first three fused results. Article 21 wins because both rankers put it near the top.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-shrike.git
cd blyx-shrike
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A keyword ranker and an embedding ranker return scores on different scales. Reciprocal rank fusion combines each document’s position in the lists. It gives a developer an inspectable baseline before tuning a score calibration or training a reranker.

reference.title: Cormack, Clarke and Buettcher, Reciprocal Rank Fusion

packages.logoAlt: A black-masked shrike turns its small hooked bill.

packages.name: blyx-bunting
packages.title: Bunting
packages.description: Publish a distribution as a standalone HTML table with interval labels, counts and meters. Reuse the same bin definitions in reports and tests.
packages.contract: Supply finite strictly increasing boundaries. A value exactly on a boundary belongs to the bucket above it. Bucket −1 counts missing or non-finite values. An empty boundary vector represents all finite values. The table generator validates boundaries before writing any markup. The caller supplies the HTML document around the table.
api: bu_valid(edges), bu_bucket(edges, value)
Check boundaries and locate the value by binary search.
bu_count(data, edges, bucket)
Count observations in one bucket. An invalid request returns −1.
bu_table(data, edges)
Write a captioned HTML table with explicit counts and meter values. Returns false for invalid boundaries.

workflow.title: Publish a support-queue report
workflow.description: Group eight first-reply waits at 5, 10 and 20 minutes. The resulting HTML page opens offline and exposes intervals, counts and shares as a table. Every observation contributes to one row.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bunting.git
cd blyx-bunting
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A colored chart alone can hide values from people navigating with assistive technology. W3C’s table guidance pairs data cells with headers. Bunting emits row and column headers and prints the count alongside every meter.

reference.title: W3C WAI, Tables with One Header

packages.logoAlt: A painted bunting with a cobalt head, red breast and green wing.

packages.name: blyx-wren
packages.title: Wren
packages.description: Run named checks and skips, compare floating-point measurements, and report a TAP 13 stream and a process exit status for CI.
packages.contract: Start with wr_begin, pass the returned suite to each check or skip, then call process_exit(wr_end(suite)). The producer emits a trailing TAP plan. Names are truncated at a line break or # to keep the stream unambiguous. Relative tolerance ranges from zero to one. Inputs for measurements and tolerances must be finite.
api: wr_begin(), wr_check(suite, passed, label)
Import tap. Start a TAP stream and record numbered checks.
wr_skip(suite, label, detail), wr_end(suite)
Declare a skip and finish with a plan. wr_end returns 1 when a check failed.
wr_near(actual, expected, absolute, relative)
Compare using the larger of an absolute tolerance and a tolerance scaled by the larger input magnitude.
wr_start(), wr_record(suite, passed, skipped), wr_exit(suite)
Track total, failed and skipped cases without writing TAP output.

workflow.title: Test an invoice and packing calculation
workflow.description: The suite checks a decimal invoice total and a whole-box count, then records an offline printer as a skip. Change the expected box count to see the process exit with status 1.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-wren.git
cd blyx-wren
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A test that only prints an error can leave a build green. TAP defines a machine-readable result for each check and a plan stating how many results to expect. Wren couples that output to the number of failures.

packages.logoAlt: A chestnut wren with a cream eyebrow holds its striped tail upright.

packages.name: blyx-weaver
packages.title: Weaver
packages.description: Lay out equal-width tiles on small or large viewports, distribute leftover pixels and map pointer coordinates back to an item.
packages.contract: Use integer logical pixels. Width, inset, gap, minimum width and row height support values up to 1,000,000. The column limit is 1–10,000, and a grid can address 1,000,000 items. Invalid geometry produces an empty rectangle or a missed hit. Right and bottom edges are exclusive. A narrow positive content area uses one column.
api: we_columns(width, inset, gap, minimum, limit)
Choose a responsive column count; zero indicates an empty or invalid content area.
we_rect(width, inset, gap, columns, rowHeight, index)
Return [x, y, width, height] in logical pixels.
we_hit(width, inset, gap, columns, rowHeight, count, x, y)
Find the item under a pointer. Gutters, empty cells and outside positions return −1.

workflow.title: Render a file chooser as SVG
workflow.description: The example draws five file tiles in three columns. The final row has two items. Use the same geometry for touch or mouse hit testing when embedding the layout in a UI host.
workflow.browserTitle: Lay out and hit-test five tiles
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-weaver.git
cd blyx-weaver
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A grid can draw a tile in one place and dispatch a click to its neighbor if painting and input code round dimensions differently. CSS Grid describes how tracks and gaps form a layout. Weaver uses one integer track calculation for both drawing and input.

reference.title: W3C, CSS Grid Layout Module Level 1

packages.logoAlt: A golden masked weaver grips a green reed in its bill.

packages.name: blyx-dipper
packages.title: Dipper
packages.description: Parse quoted CSV records, preserve embedded line breaks, and validate a row width before consuming a file.
packages.contract: Parse a UTF-8 string in memory. Delimiters are commas. Records accept CRLF, LF or CR; embedded quoted newlines preserve their original bytes. Spaces are data. A malformed quote discards partial results. Empty input contains zero rows; a blank line holds one empty cell. di_bad_row applies a caller-supplied column count.
api: di_parse(input), di_ok(records)
Import csv. Parse into F-prefixed field events and R end-of-row events. A lone E-prefixed event describes a syntax error.
di_cell(records, row, column)
Return one string for a present cell, including an empty cell; an absent cell returns an empty list.
di_bad_row(records, width)
Return the first zero-based row of the wrong width, −1 for success or −2 for a parse or argument error.
di_transition(state, token), di_shape(tokens)
Walk the portable quote state machine. A valid stream yields [rows, fields].

workflow.title: Import a two-column notes file
workflow.description: The importer preserves a literal quote in the first note and an embedded newline in the second. Give it a UTF-8 CSV file to check its width before reading the note column.
workflow.browserTitle: Trace the CSV parser through quoted fields
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dipper.git
cd blyx-dipper
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: Splitting each line on commas changes both field contents and record counts when a field contains a quoted comma or newline. RFC 4180 describes the quoting and doubled-quote rules that the Dipper parser uses.

reference.title: RFC 4180, Common Format and MIME Type for CSV Files

packages.logoAlt: A round brown dipper with a white breast leans towards a ripple.

packages.name: blyx-kestrel
packages.title: Kestrel
packages.description: Run a bounded number of simulation ticks per rendered frame, carry fractional frame time and interpolate a moving object between updates.
packages.contract: Use whole milliseconds from 0 to 1,000,000,000, a positive step and a remainder smaller than that step. max_steps is 1–1,000,000. The clock returns an empty vector for invalid input. A frame cap discards whole ticks only. The simulation takes frame durations from the caller so a replay needs no wall clock.
api: ke_clock(carry, elapsed, step, max_steps)
Return [updates, remainder_ms, discarded_ms, interpolation_fraction]. Feed remainder_ms into the next frame.
ke_lerp(previous, current, fraction)
Interpolate a render position between the last two simulated positions.
ke_bounce(position, velocity, dt, low, high)
Advance one object on a bounded 1D track. The result holds position and velocity, including repeated wall crossings.

workflow.title: Replay a bouncing ball across a stalled frame
workflow.description: Feed the same five frame times into a fixed-step ball simulation. One 100 ms stall exceeds the catch-up limit. The replay reports positions and the number of milliseconds discarded.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kestrel.git
cd blyx-kestrel
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: Rendering at a changing frame rate can change simulation speed. A long pause can also produce a burst of catch-up work. Godot’s physics interpolation guide explains the separate clocks. Kestrel makes the carry, interpolation fraction and discarded time visible to the application.

reference.title: Godot Engine, Introduction to physics interpolation

packages.logoAlt: A russet and blue-grey kestrel hovers with its tail spread.

packages.name: blyx-heron
packages.title: Heron
packages.description: Track one sensor feed’s accepted messages, duplicate sequence numbers, out-of-order arrivals and missed deadlines.
packages.contract: Maintain one state per sensor. Use a monotonically increasing integer sequence and a monotonic local receipt clock in milliseconds, both at most 2^53−1. Reset the state when the sensor restarts or its sequence wraps. The gap counter records skipped IDs at acceptance time. Late arrivals do not reduce it. This release monitors application data and exposes its state to the host.
api: he_start(), he_observe(state, sequence, receipt_ms)
Initialize or update [last sequence, last receipt, accepted, duplicates, out of order, skipped IDs].
he_age(state, now)
Return milliseconds since the latest accepted observation, or −1 when unavailable.
he_status(state, now, deadline)
Return unseen, current, late or invalid. A reading remains current exactly at its deadline.

workflow.title: Audit a sensor heartbeat trace
workflow.description: Replay sequence and local receipt-time pairs. The bundled trace contains a duplicate, a two-ID gap and one out-of-order delivery. You can feed your own two-column headerless trace into the same program.
workflow.browserTitle: Detect an expired feed after a duplicate
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-heron.git
cd blyx-heron
blyxc native-run project.blyx
workflow.problem: A replayed packet can make an idle sensor appear healthy if every arrival resets its last-seen timer. ROS 2 distinguishes delivery and deadline policies. Heron lets an application choose a freshness deadline and updates that timer only when it accepts a new sample.

packages.logoAlt: A blue heron folds its neck and points its golden bill forward.

packages.name: blyx-releasewindow
packages.title: ReleaseWindow
packages.description: Locate a clock tick within a scheduled publication window.
packages.contract: Returns [phase, ticks until the next change]. Phase 0 is scheduled, 1 is live and 2 is expired. The closing tick is exclusive. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: releasewindow_locate(now, opens, closes)
Returns [phase, ticks until the next change]. Phase 0 is scheduled, 1 is live and 2 is expired. The closing tick is exclusive.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin passing a publication through the open sector of a clock.

packages.name: blyx-reviewquorum
packages.title: ReviewQuorum
packages.description: Count independent reviewers and calculate outstanding approvals.
packages.contract: Returns [unique reviewer IDs, approvals still required]. A repeated ID contributes once. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: reviewquorum_tally(reviewers, required)
Returns [unique reviewer IDs, approvals still required]. A repeated ID contributes once.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin collecting distinct approval stamps on a proof sheet.

packages.name: blyx-oriole
packages.title: Oriole
packages.description: Decide whether a scheduled revision can go live after independent review.
packages.contract: Returns [publish now, lifecycle phase, approvals missing, ticks to next transition]. The caller supplies the clock and persists the revision. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: oriole_decide(now, opens, closes, reviewers, required)
Returns [publish now, lifecycle phase, approvals missing, ticks to next transition]. The caller supplies the clock and persists the revision.
packages.logoAlt: An orange-and-black oriole lifts its head above two white wing bars.

workflow.description: At tick 12 two distinct reviewers have approved the revision. A duplicate approval cannot replace the second reviewer.

Returns [lots to order, supplied units, surplus]. A zero shortage orders zero lots.

Returns [applied, still due, overpayment] in a single currency's minor units.

Returns [subtotal, applied payment, open balance, credit]. Use a single currency and already-posted amounts.

packages.name: blyx-exitpolicy
packages.title: ExitPolicy
packages.description: Summarize portable process exit codes without losing the first failure.
packages.contract: Returns [failed commands, first nonzero exit code, first failing index]. An all-success run uses index -1. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: exitpolicy_summarize(codes)

workflow.title: Score detections at the edge of a camera frame

workflow.title: Distinguish a clipped transient from a sustained overload

workflow.title: Bridge short pauses in a speech-activity trace

workflow.title: Cover a survey that crosses a grid origin

packages.logoAlt: A charcoal storm petrel touches a wave with its yellow feet.

workflow.title: Decide whether a queued request can afford to wait
workflow.description: The bucket has four tokens and needs eight. At two tokens per tick the charge fits the two-tick deadline.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-petrel.git

blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 2 10 2 1 8 2
workflow.problem: Charging a delayed request immediately can remove capacity from unrelated work. Return the wait separately from the updated balance.

packages.name: blyx-offsetgap
packages.title: OffsetGap
packages.description: Audit an ordered offset trace against an expected starting value.
packages.contract: Returns [forward gaps counted at first observation, stale or replayed deliveries, next high-water offset]. Late arrivals do not erase earlier gaps. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.

Returns [forward gaps counted at first observation, stale or replayed deliveries, next high-water offset]. Late arrivals do not erase earlier gaps.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin finding a missing block in a sequence of delivery offsets.

packages.name: blyx-ackprefix
packages.title: AckPrefix
packages.description: Find the longest contiguous acknowledgement prefix in unordered deliveries.
packages.contract: Returns [next unacknowledged offset, advanced count]. Duplicate acknowledgements never advance the cursor twice. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: ackprefix_advance(acked, start)
Returns [next unacknowledged offset, advanced count]. Duplicate acknowledgements never advance the cursor twice.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin clasping a consecutive run of acknowledged envelopes.

packages.name: blyx-fulmar
packages.title: Fulmar
packages.description: Choose a contiguous commit offset from an out-of-order delivery trace.

api: fulmar_checkpoint(delivered, acked, start)
Returns [next commit, observed gaps, stale deliveries, per-trace high water]. Acknowledgements at or beyond start must refer to delivered offsets in this trace.
packages.logoAlt: A grey and white fulmar glides with its wings held level.

workflow.title: Commit offsets without skipping unfinished deliveries
workflow.description: Acknowledging offsets 4 and 6 advances the cursor only to 5. Offset 6 can remain acknowledged until 5 completes.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-fulmar.git
cd blyx-fulmar
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "4,6,5,6" "4,6" 4
workflow.problem: Committing the largest acknowledged offset can skip a message that is still in flight. Advance only through a contiguous prefix.

packages.name: blyx-querydepth
packages.title: QueryDepth
packages.description: Validate a preorder field-depth trace from an expanded query plan.
packages.contract: Returns [maximum depth, root fields, total fields]. Depth starts at one. A child can descend only one level; siblings and ascent are allowed. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: querydepth_shape(depths)
Returns [maximum depth, root fields, total fields]. Depth starts at one. A child can descend only one level; siblings and ascent are allowed.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin lowering a plumb line through a tree of query fields.

packages.name: blyx-fieldcost
packages.title: FieldCost
packages.description: Estimate expanded resolver work using per-field costs and visit counts.
packages.contract: Returns [total work, costliest field index, largest single field contribution]. Empty input uses index -1. Inputs come from the host query planner. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: fieldcost_weighted(units, visits)
Returns [total work, costliest field index, largest single field contribution]. Empty input uses index -1. Inputs come from the host query planner.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin weighing a branching field diagram against visit counters.

packages.name: blyx-waxwing
packages.title: Waxwing
packages.description: Check the depth and weighted resolver cost of an expanded GraphQL field plan.
packages.contract: Returns [admitted, maximum depth, total work, costliest field index]. Supply resolved aliases, fragments and list visit estimates from your parser. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: waxwing_budget(depths, units, visits, max_depth, budget)
Returns [admitted, maximum depth, total work, costliest field index]. Supply resolved aliases, fragments and list visit estimates from your parser.
packages.logoAlt: A crested cinnamon waxwing with a black mask and red wing tips.

workflow.title: Budget an expanded GraphQL field plan
workflow.description: The plan is only two levels deep, but its visit-weighted work is 17 against a budget of 15.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-waxwing.git
cd blyx-waxwing
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,2,2" "1,3,2" "1,4,2" 3 15
workflow.problem: A flat query can cost more than a deep one when list fields fan out. Evaluate expanded cost and depth independently.

packages.name: blyx-deadlinepath
packages.title: DeadlinePath
packages.description: Propagate a parent time budget across elapsed RPC stages.
packages.contract: Returns [usable child budget, overrun after reserve, elapsed total]. Durations use one clock unit. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: deadlinepath_remaining(budget, stages, reserve)
Returns [usable child budget, overrun after reserve, elapsed total]. Durations use one clock unit.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin carrying a shrinking time budget through relay rings.

packages.name: blyx-statusretry
packages.title: StatusRetry
packages.description: Check a conservative retry policy for selected gRPC status codes.
packages.contract: Returns [retry eligible, attempts remaining]. Retries require an idempotent operation, a remaining attempt, and status 14 (UNAVAILABLE) or 4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). Status is in 0–16. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: statusretry_classify(status, idempotent, attempts, max_attempts)
Returns [retry eligible, attempts remaining]. Retries require an idempotent operation, a remaining attempt, and status 14 (UNAVAILABLE) or 4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED). Status is in 0–16.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin sending one status token around a retry loop and stopping another.

packages.name: blyx-martin
packages.title: Martin
packages.description: Decide whether another RPC attempt fits the remaining end-to-end deadline.
packages.contract: Returns [retry now or after wait, attempt budget after wait, attempts left]. The minimum is the shortest useful child duration. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: martin_retry(budget, stages, wait, minimum, status, idempotent, attempts, limit)
Returns [retry now or after wait, attempt budget after wait, attempts left]. The minimum is the shortest useful child duration.
packages.logoAlt: A blue-and-white house martin arcs through the air on pointed wings.

workflow.title: Fit a retry into an RPC deadline
workflow.description: Fifty ticks have elapsed and ten are reserved for backoff. An idempotent retry has forty ticks available.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-martin.git
cd blyx-martin
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 100 "20,30" 10 35 14 1 1 3
workflow.problem: Resetting a timeout at each hop lets a retry outlive its caller. Subtract already-spent time and the coming backoff.

packages.name: blyx-byterange
packages.title: ByteRange
packages.description: Resolve a single inclusive HTTP byte range to an offset and length.
packages.contract: Returns [satisfiable, offset, length]. Set last to -1 for an open-ended range. A syntactically reversed range is invalid. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: byterange_resolve(size, first, last)
Returns [satisfiable, offset, length]. Set last to -1 for an open-ended range. A syntactically reversed range is invalid.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin clamping both ends of a selected middle segment of a byte strip.

packages.name: blyx-suffixrange
packages.title: SuffixRange
packages.description: Resolve an HTTP suffix-byte specification without negative offsets.
packages.contract: Returns [satisfiable, offset, length]. A suffix longer than the entity selects the full entity. Zero bytes or an empty entity produce an unsatisfied range. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: suffixrange_resolve(size, suffix)
Returns [satisfiable, offset, length]. A suffix longer than the entity selects the full entity. Zero bytes or an empty entity produce an unsatisfied range.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin gathering the final blocks at the end of a rolled byte strip.

packages.name: blyx-kinglet
packages.title: Kinglet
packages.description: Plan a full or single-range HTTP response against a known representation size.
packages.contract: Returns [status, body offset, body length, full length]. Mode 0 sends the full body, 1 uses first/last, 2 uses first as a suffix count. Header parsing and multipart ranges belong to the host. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: kinglet_respond(size, mode, first, last)
Returns [status, body offset, body length, full length]. Mode 0 sends the full body, 1 uses first/last, 2 uses first as a suffix count. Header parsing and multipart ranges belong to the host.
packages.logoAlt: A small olive kinglet looks up beneath a brilliant gold crown.

workflow.title: Serve a byte range at end of file
workflow.description: A request for bytes 90 through 200 of a 100-byte resource returns ten bytes beginning at 90.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-kinglet.git
cd blyx-kinglet
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 100 1 90 200
workflow.problem: An inclusive last byte becomes a read length with a plus one. Handle suffixes, empty resources and unsatisfied offsets explicitly.

packages.name: blyx-eventorder
packages.title: EventOrder
packages.description: Locate time-order anomalies in a log stream in receipt order.
packages.contract: Returns [adjacent clock reversals, largest backward step, first reversal index]. Equal timestamps preserve order. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: eventorder_scan(times)
Returns [adjacent clock reversals, largest backward step, first reversal index]. Equal timestamps preserve order.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin lifting an out-of-order clock tile from a row of log entries.

packages.name: blyx-auditgaps
packages.title: AuditGaps
packages.description: Count forward gaps and nonadvancing IDs in an audit export.
packages.contract: Returns [missing at first observation, nonadvancing rows, highest observed ID]. The first row establishes the baseline; the empty sentinel is -1. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: auditgaps_sequence(ids)
Returns [missing at first observation, nonadvancing rows, highest observed ID]. The first row establishes the baseline; the empty sentinel is -1.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin inspecting a punched audit strip for missing and repeated marks.

packages.name: blyx-barnowl
packages.title: Barnowl
packages.description: Inspect a supplied audit export for sequence gaps, replays and clock reversals.
packages.contract: Returns [gap count, nonadvancing IDs, backward clock steps, first reversed row, clean flag]. Preserve original receipt order; a gap is an observation for investigation. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: barnowl_audit(ids, times)
Returns [gap count, nonadvancing IDs, backward clock steps, first reversed row, clean flag]. Preserve original receipt order; a gap is an observation for investigation.
packages.logoAlt: A copper barn owl tilts its heart-shaped white face.

workflow.title: Find clock reversals and gaps in an audit export
workflow.description: The sample skips sequence 41, repeats 42 and ends with a backward clock step. The result identifies the reversed row.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-barnowl.git
cd blyx-barnowl
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "40,42,42" "10,14,12"
workflow.problem: Sorting an export by timestamp can conceal a clock rollback. Audit receipt order and sequence continuity as separate signals.

packages.name: blyx-claimclock
packages.title: ClaimClock
packages.description: Evaluate activation and expiration bounds on previously verified claims.
packages.contract: Returns [time accepted, early ticks, expired ticks]. Expiration is exclusive and applies symmetric caller-supplied clock tolerance. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: claimclock_check(now, begins, expires, skew)
Returns [time accepted, early ticks, expired ticks]. Expiration is exclusive and applies symmetric caller-supplied clock tolerance.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin checking a verified pass against a clock’s validity window.

packages.name: blyx-assurancelevel
packages.title: AssuranceLevel
packages.description: Check session freshness and an application-defined ordered assurance level.
packages.contract: Returns [meets both, age, missing assurance levels]. A future authentication time is invalid; equality at the age limit is accepted. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: assurancelevel_policy(observed, required, auth_time, now, max_age)
Returns [meets both, age, missing assurance levels]. A future authentication time is invalid; equality at the age limit is accepted.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin raising an identity pass to the required assurance rung.

packages.name: blyx-harrier
packages.title: Harrier
packages.description: Apply time and assurance policy to a session after upstream identity verification.
packages.contract: Returns [policy accepted, claims time accepted, assurance/freshness accepted, session age]. Use only after the host has authenticated and verified the issuer, audience and signature. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: harrier_session(now, begins, expires, skew, observed, required, auth_time, max_age)
Returns [policy accepted, claims time accepted, assurance/freshness accepted, session age]. Use only after the host has authenticated and verified the issuer, audience and signature.
packages.logoAlt: A silver-grey harrier glides on black-tipped wings.

workflow.title: Apply freshness policy to a verified session
workflow.description: The verified session is eight ticks old and meets the required assurance level. The expiration boundary remains exclusive.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-harrier.git
cd blyx-harrier
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 100 90 110 0 2 2 92 10
workflow.problem: A still-valid token can represent an old or insufficiently verified session. Apply application policy after the identity provider has verified the token.

packages.name: blyx-sloburn
packages.title: SloBurn
packages.description: Normalize observed failures by an allowed error fraction.
packages.contract: Returns [observed error fraction, burn multiple]. The allowed error fraction is greater than zero and at most one. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: sloburn_rate(bad, total, allowed)
Returns [observed error fraction, burn multiple]. The allowed error fraction is greater than zero and at most one.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin reading a gauge as an error budget burns.

packages.name: blyx-budgetleft
packages.title: BudgetLeft
packages.description: Account for whole allowed failures in an observed window.
packages.contract: Returns [whole failures permitted, remaining, excess]. Rounds the nonnegative product of sample count and allowance down. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: budgetleft_events(bad, total, allowance)
Returns [whole failures permitted, remaining, excess]. Rounds the nonnegative product of sample count and allowance down.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin separating spent counters from the remaining error budget.

packages.name: blyx-plover
packages.title: Plover
packages.description: Gate alerts on error-budget burn in both a short and a long window.
packages.contract: Returns [alert, short burn, long burn, long-window excess failures]. The short window must be a subset of the long window, including its good events. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: plover_alert(fast_bad, fast_total, slow_bad, slow_total, allowed, trigger)
Returns [alert, short burn, long burn, long-window excess failures]. The short window must be a subset of the long window, including its good events.
packages.logoAlt: A sandy plover stands upright with a dark band across its breast.

workflow.title: Gate an alert on short and long error windows
workflow.description: The short window burns four times its error budget and the long window burns twice. Both reach the selected threshold.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-plover.git
cd blyx-plover
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 2 10 10 100 0.05 2
workflow.problem: A brief burst or stale long-window average can trigger a noisy alert on its own. Require both windows to cross the selected burn threshold.

reference.title: Google SRE Workbook, alerting on SLOs

packages.name: blyx-stratamean
packages.title: StrataMean
packages.description: Pool event counts and expose the crude observed rate.

Returns [total events, total trials, crude rate]. Every stratum must have observations and events cannot exceed trials.

packages.name: blyx-stdweight
packages.title: StdWeight
packages.description: Directly standardize stratum-specific rates to a reference population.

Returns [standardized rate, total reference weight]. Positive-weight strata require observations. Zero-weight strata may be empty.

packages.name: blyx-jacana
packages.title: Jacana
packages.description: Compare a crude event rate with a directly standardized rate.

Returns [crude rate, standardized rate, standardized minus crude, total observations]. Each reported stratum needs observations for the crude comparison. Causal interpretation depends on study design.
packages.logoAlt: A chestnut jacana with a red forehead spreads its toes over a lily pad.

workflow.title: Compare a crude rate with a standardized rate
workflow.description: The crude event rate is 0.75. Equal reference weights give each stratum the same influence and reduce the standardized rate to 0.5.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.1 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-jacana.git
cd blyx-jacana
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,6" "2,6" "1,1"
workflow.problem: A change in the mix of observed groups can move the pooled rate. Recalculate rates against fixed reference weights before comparing populations.

packages.name: blyx-betaupdate

packages.name: blyx-betamoment

api: betamoment_summary(alpha, beta)
Returns [mean, variance, concentration]. Uses mean times its complement divided by concentration plus one.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin marking the center and spread of a probability curve.

packages.name: blyx-redstart

Returns [posterior mean, posterior variance, posterior alpha, posterior beta]. This conjugate model assumes exchangeable Bernoulli observations.

workflow.title: Update a binary-event probability after observations
workflow.description: One success and one failure update a uniform prior to Beta(2,2). The posterior mean is 0.5 and its variance is 0.05.

blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 1 1 1 1
workflow.problem: A point estimate alone hides the difference between two observations and two thousand. Return posterior variance with the updated mean.

packages.name: blyx-quail

Returns [predicted P(1), observed P(1), absolute discrepancy]. Gates are applied left to right. Complex phase gates and hardware execution require a different state representation.

workflow.title: Compare a real-qubit circuit with observed shots
workflow.description: The X and Z sequence prepares a state whose probability of one is 1. Six ones in eight measured shots give a 0.25 discrepancy.

Bin order is 00,01,10,11. Returns [even frequency, odd frequency, parity expectation]. At least one shot is required.

Bin order is 00,01,10,11. Returns [P(left=1), P(right=1), shots]. At least one shot is required.

Returns [parity expectation, left-one frequency, right-one frequency, parity matches target]. A single measurement basis characterizes this histogram only.

workflow.title: Read parity alongside two-bit marginals

Returns [signed integral, signed span]. A descending grid reverses the integral sign. At least two paired samples are required.

packages.name: blyx-gridgap

Returns [largest absolute step, right index of the first largest step, nonincreasing steps]. At least two points are required.

packages.name: blyx-magpie

workflow.title: Integrate unevenly spaced observations

packages.name: blyx-axisrange

api: axisrange_extent(samples, zero)
Returns [lower, upper]. Set zero to 1 to include the origin. A constant domain receives ±0.5 or ±5% of its magnitude, whichever is larger.

packages.name: blyx-tickstep

packages.description: Choose a covering linear tick lattice using steps 1, 2, 5 or 10 times a power of ten.

api: tickstep_cover(lo, hi, intervals)
Returns [first tick, last tick, step, tick count]. Interval count is a target. Supported raw steps range from 1e-100 to 1e100.

workflow.title: Choose chart ticks for an observed range

Returns [can apply next, next available version, pending count, changed fingerprints]. This preflight consumes an exported history and executes no SQL.

workflow.title: Decide whether the next database migration can run
workflow.description: The two applied versions form an exact prefix with matching fingerprints. Version 5 is ready to apply.

Returns [first index, exclusive end, resume key, has more]. On an empty result the input cursor is retained. Supply stable unique numeric keys from a consistent snapshot.

workflow.title: Resume a keyset page from its last emitted key
workflow.description: A cursor between keys selects 20 and 30. Returning 30 lets the next page start at 40.

blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "10,20,30,40" 15 2

packages.name: blyx-foreignmiss

Returns [orphan rows, first orphan row]. Repeated child references are checked independently; represent missing/null separately.

workflow.title: Audit a parent and child table before import
workflow.description: The parent export repeats ID 1. Two child rows reference the missing ID 2.

git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-dunlin.git
cd blyx-dunlin
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,1,3" "1,2,2"

packages.name: blyx-freshclock
packages.title: FreshClock

Returns [current age, remaining freshness, stale age]. Supply corrected initial age. Equality with freshness lifetime is stale.

packages.name: blyx-stalewindow
packages.title: StaleWindow
packages.description: Classify a cache entry under an explicit stale-serving policy.

api: stalewindow_classify(age, lifetime, grace, mandatory)
Returns [mode, ticks remaining in current window]. Mode 0 is fresh, 1 is stale within grace, 2 requires validation. Mandatory validation disables grace for stale entries.

packages.name: blyx-sanderling
packages.title: Sanderling

api: sanderling_lookup(age_at_store, stored, now, lifetime, grace, mandatory)
Returns [mode, current age, ticks until mode changes]. Mode 0 serves fresh, 1 serves under explicit stale grace, and 2 requires validation. The host parses and enforces other cache directives.
packages.logoAlt: A silver-white sanderling runs on short dark legs.

workflow.title: Carry cache age across a local storage interval
workflow.description: An entry stored at age eight reaches age thirteen after five more ticks. Three ticks of its stale-serving grace remain.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-sanderling.git
cd blyx-sanderling
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 8 100 105 10 6 0
workflow.problem: Starting freshness at zero on every cache hop can keep stale content alive. Carry the stored age forward before applying grace.

packages.name: blyx-transitspan

Returns [minimum arrival minus send, maximum, backward arrival steps]. Times use the same tick unit and a stable offset between clocks.

packages.name: blyx-jittermean
packages.title: JitterMean

Returns [updated jitter, adjacent pairs]. Supply arrival-order packets in the same unwrapped timestamp units; the first observation establishes transit.

packages.name: blyx-cormorant
packages.title: Cormorant

Returns [transit range, smoothed jitter, adjacent pairs]. Input rows must be in arrival order and use unwrapped sender timestamps.
packages.logoAlt: A dark cormorant with a turquoise eye extends one wet wing.

workflow.title: Separate packet jitter from a fixed clock offset
workflow.description: Transit changes by 32 ticks. Starting from zero, the one-sixteenth update yields two ticks of smoothed jitter.

blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,16" "100,148" 0

workflow.title: Validate required and extra object fields

packages.name: blyx-optionlayer

Returns [unsigned checksum, rolling low accumulator, rolling high accumulator]. The empty digest is 1. Use for accidental corruption detection.

workflow.title: Verify a record table before interpreting a byte offset

packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin counting completed calendar years before a January bookmark.

packages.name: blyx-robin
packages.title: Robin
packages.description: Convert a validated civil date into an ordinal, weekday and comparable day number.
packages.contract: Returns [day number with 0001-01-01 = 1, Monday-zero weekday, day-of-year, days in month]. This is a calendar computation independent of machine locale. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: robin_date(year, month, day)
Returns [day number with 0001-01-01 = 1, Monday-zero weekday, day-of-year, days in month]. This is a calendar computation independent of machine locale.
packages.logoAlt: An olive-brown robin lifts its head above a round orange breast.

workflow.title: Convert a civil date into comparable day numbers
workflow.description: January 1, 1970 has day number 719163 and Monday-zero weekday 3. Century years follow the full Gregorian leap rule.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-robin.git
cd blyx-robin
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 1970 1 1
workflow.problem: Month lengths and century leap rules affect both date validation and weekday calculations. Resolve both from the same Gregorian day number.

packages.name: blyx-intervalunion
packages.title: IntervalUnion
packages.description: Measure union length and coverage components of sorted half-open intervals.
packages.contract: Returns [covered ticks, connected components, enclosing span]. Touching intervals are merged. Empty input has zero span. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: intervalunion_measure(starts, ends)
Returns [covered ticks, connected components, enclosing span]. Touching intervals are merged. Empty input has zero span.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin joining overlapping time ribbons into one covered span.

packages.name: blyx-peakslots
packages.title: PeakSlots
packages.description: Find peak simultaneous occupancy of half-open intervals.
packages.contract: Returns [peak active intervals, earliest tick at that peak]. Empty input returns [0,0]. Counts exactly at starts, where occupancy can increase; short batches use quadratic time. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: peakslots_overlap(starts, ends)
Returns [peak active intervals, earliest tick at that peak]. Empty input returns [0,0]. Counts exactly at starts, where occupancy can increase; short batches use quadratic time.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin counting bookings stacked over the same time slot.

packages.name: blyx-starling
packages.title: Starling
packages.description: Estimate resource capacity and actual occupied time from a booking schedule.
packages.contract: Returns [covered ticks, peak simultaneous bookings, earliest peak, capacity shortfall]. Starts must be sorted; adjacent bookings can share a resource. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: starling_capacity(starts, ends, capacity)
Returns [covered ticks, peak simultaneous bookings, earliest peak, capacity shortfall]. Starts must be sorted; adjacent bookings can share a resource.
packages.logoAlt: An emerald and violet starling shows pale spots and a yellow bill.

workflow.title: Size a resource pool from overlapping bookings
workflow.description: Three bookings cover seven ticks and reach two simultaneous users. A pool of one is short by one resource.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-starling.git
cd blyx-starling
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,2,4" "4,5,7" 1
workflow.problem: Summing all booking durations double-counts overlap. Measure occupied time separately from peak resource demand.

packages.name: blyx-civiloffset
packages.title: CivilOffset
packages.description: Convert a local tick to a candidate UTC tick for a supplied offset.
packages.contract: Returns [candidate UTC, offset]. Offsets use seconds and must lie strictly within ±24 hours. Local ticks use the same epoch and unit. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: civiloffset_candidate(local, offset)
Returns [candidate UTC, offset]. Offsets use seconds and must lie strictly within ±24 hours. Local ticks use the same epoch and unit.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin converting between linked local and universal clock faces.

packages.name: blyx-clockfold
packages.title: ClockFold
packages.description: Classify a local time around one supplied offset transition.
packages.contract: Returns [number of valid UTC candidates, earliest candidate, latest candidate]. A forward gap yields [0,0,0]; a backward fold yields two candidates. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: clockfold_classify(local, transition, before, after)
Returns [number of valid UTC candidates, earliest candidate, latest candidate]. A forward gap yields [0,0,0]; a backward fold yields two candidates.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin opening a folded clock to reveal two possible instants.

packages.name: blyx-blackbird
packages.title: Blackbird
packages.description: Resolve a wall-clock timestamp at a known gap or fold without guessing its offset.
packages.contract: Returns [candidate count, selected UTC, selected offset]. For a gap the latter two values are zero. Fold 0 chooses the earlier occurrence and fold 1 the later. Supply transition data from a trusted timezone database. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: blackbird_resolve(local, transition, before, after, fold)

Returns [candidate count, selected UTC, selected offset]. For a gap the latter two values are zero. Fold 0 chooses the earlier occurrence and fold 1 the later. Supply transition data from a trusted timezone database.
packages.logoAlt: A charcoal blackbird tilts its head, showing an orange eye ring and bill.

workflow.title: Resolve both occurrences of an ambiguous wall time
workflow.description: After the offset moves back, local tick 11000 has two UTC candidates. Fold 1 selects the later occurrence.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-blackbird.git
cd blyx-blackbird
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- 11000 10000 3600 0 1
workflow.problem: One wall time can occur twice during a fall-back transition and disappear entirely during a forward jump. Expose the number of valid UTC candidates.

packages.name: blyx-indentsteps
packages.title: IndentSteps
packages.description: Audit fixed-step indentation measured on nonblank source lines.
packages.contract: Returns [off-grid or illegal jump count, first offending row, deepest column]. The first nonblank row starts at zero and one line can increase by at most one indent step. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: indentsteps_audit(indent, step)
Returns [off-grid or illegal jump count, first offending row, deepest column]. The first nonblank row starts at zero and one line can increase by at most one indent step.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin checking indented lines against a stepped square.

packages.name: blyx-linewidth
packages.title: LineWidth
packages.description: Find overlong source lines from measured display columns.
packages.contract: Returns [overlong rows, first overlong row, largest excess]. The host selects a Unicode display-width convention and supplies widths including indentation. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: linewidth_audit(widths, limit)
Returns [overlong rows, first overlong row, largest excess]. The host selects a Unicode display-width convention and supplies widths including indentation.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin flagging the line that crosses a display-width ruler.

packages.name: blyx-towhee
packages.title: Towhee
packages.description: Combine indentation and line-width diagnostics for a measured source file.
packages.contract: Returns [clean, indentation violations, overlong rows, first problem row]. Supply aligned nonblank physical lines and their display widths. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: towhee_lint(indent, widths, step, limit)
Returns [clean, indentation violations, overlong rows, first problem row]. Supply aligned nonblank physical lines and their display widths.
packages.logoAlt: A black-hooded towhee with rust flanks scratches backwards with one foot.

workflow.title: Locate the first actionable source-style violation
workflow.description: The second line exceeds its width limit and the third makes an illegal indentation jump. The first problem is zero-based row 1.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-towhee.git
cd blyx-towhee
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,4,12" "60,88,70" 4 80
workflow.problem: A line can have acceptable length but invalid indentation. Preserve both counts and show the earliest actionable row.

packages.name: blyx-semvercore
packages.title: SemVerCore
packages.description: Compare two numeric semantic-version cores lexicographically.
packages.contract: Both inputs are [major, minor, patch]. Returns [ordering (-1,0,1), first differing component or -1]. Prerelease identifiers and build metadata are outside this core. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: semvercore_compare(left, right)
Both inputs are [major, minor, patch]. Returns [ordering (-1,0,1), first differing component or -1]. Prerelease identifiers and build metadata are outside this core.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin pointing to the first differing drum on two version counters.

packages.name: blyx-versionband
packages.title: VersionBand
packages.description: Check membership of a numeric-version core in a half-open dependency interval.
packages.contract: Returns [inside, below lower, at or above upper]. All versions have three integer components and lower must precede upper. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: versionband_contains(version, lower, upper)
Returns [inside, below lower, at or above upper]. All versions have three integer components and lower must precede upper.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin placing a version tag between a filled and an open endpoint.

packages.name: blyx-bowerbird
packages.title: Bowerbird
packages.description: Decide whether a proposed numeric-core dependency upgrade fits a declared version range.
packages.contract: Returns [allowed upgrade, candidate versus installed, major/minor/patch index changed, within range]. Equal versions are allowed. This release handles numeric cores and explicit bounds. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: bowerbird_upgrade(installed, candidate, lower, upper)
Returns [allowed upgrade, candidate versus installed, major/minor/patch index changed, within range]. Equal versions are allowed. This release handles numeric cores and explicit bounds.
packages.logoAlt: A deep blue bowerbird selects a small blue petal with its pale bill.

workflow.title: Check a proposed dependency upgrade numerically
workflow.description: Version 1.10.0 follows 1.2.9 and fits the interval below 2.0.0. The first changed component is minor.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-bowerbird.git
cd blyx-bowerbird
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,2,9" "1,10,0" "1,0,0" "2,0,0"
workflow.problem: String sorting places 1.10 before 1.2. Check numeric ordering and the consumer's upper bound separately.

packages.name: blyx-dagorder
packages.title: DagOrder
packages.description: Validate indexed dependencies in an ordered build forest.
packages.contract: Each stage names one earlier parent or -1 for a root. Returns [root count, maximum chain length in stages, first stage with that depth]. Empty forests have zero depth. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: dagorder_forest(parents)
Each stage names one earlier parent or -1 for a root. Returns [root count, maximum chain length in stages, first stage with that depth]. Empty forests have zero depth.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin arranging parent and child tasks in dependency order.

packages.name: blyx-runduration
packages.title: RunDuration
packages.description: Find the critical-path time in a forest of dependent tasks.
packages.contract: Returns [longest path duration, first endpoint at that duration, total sequential work]. Each input row depends on one previous row or -1. Durations share a unit. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: runduration_path(parents, durations)
Returns [longest path duration, first endpoint at that duration, total sequential work]. Each input row depends on one previous row or -1. Durations share a unit.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin timing the longest route through a forked task network.

packages.name: blyx-albatross
packages.title: Albatross
packages.description: Estimate a build forest's scheduling lower bound from dependencies and worker capacity.
packages.contract: Returns [critical path, total work, lower bound with given workers, deepest stage count]. The capacity bound assumes divisible worker time; actual nonpreemptive schedules can take longer. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: albatross_schedule(parents, durations, workers)
Returns [critical path, total work, lower bound with given workers, deepest stage count]. The capacity bound assumes divisible worker time; actual nonpreemptive schedules can take longer.
packages.logoAlt: An ivory albatross glides diagonally on long black-tipped wings.

workflow.title: Estimate a build's critical-path lower bound
workflow.description: The four stages take eleven units of serial work. A dependency chain takes eight, so two workers cannot finish sooner than eight.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-albatross.git
cd blyx-albatross
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "-1,0,0,2" "1,3,2,5" 2
workflow.problem: Adding workers cannot shorten a serial dependency chain. Compare total work with the longest dependency path before sizing a build pool.

packages.name: blyx-sortruns
packages.title: SortRuns
packages.description: Summarize equal-value runs in a nondecreasing integer stream.
packages.contract: Returns [distinct values, longest run length, first key with that run]. Empty input returns [0,0,0]. Rejects descending keys. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: sortruns_profile(values)
Returns [distinct values, longest run length, first key with that run]. Empty input returns [0,0,0]. Rejects descending keys.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin banding the longest run of matching beads on a sorted rail.

packages.name: blyx-mergecounts
packages.title: MergeCounts
packages.description: Count unique keys shared or exclusive to two sorted streams.
packages.contract: Returns [shared, left-only, right-only]. Repeats within a stream count once. Both streams must be nondecreasing; the merge uses two forward cursors. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: mergecounts_sets(left, right)
Returns [shared, left-only, right-only]. Repeats within a stream count once. Both streams must be nondecreasing; the merge uses two forward cursors.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin combining two sorted rails and separating shared from exclusive keys.

packages.name: blyx-chaffinch
packages.title: Chaffinch
packages.description: Reconcile sorted collection snapshots without materializing their union.
packages.contract: Returns [added unique keys, removed unique keys, retained keys, duplicate occurrences in the new snapshot]. Inputs are sorted, allowing forward-only scans. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: chaffinch_reconcile(old, fresh)
Returns [added unique keys, removed unique keys, retained keys, duplicate occurrences in the new snapshot]. Inputs are sorted, allowing forward-only scans.
packages.logoAlt: A rose-breasted chaffinch shows a blue-grey crown and double white wing bars.

workflow.title: Reconcile two sorted snapshots with repeated keys
workflow.description: The new snapshot adds key 3, removes key 1 and retains 2 and 4. The repeated 2 contributes one duplicate occurrence.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-chaffinch.git
cd blyx-chaffinch
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "1,1,2,4" "2,2,3,4"
workflow.problem: A duplicate row should not look like a newly added key. Compare distinct sets and report repeated occurrences separately.

packages.name: blyx-blockspan
packages.title: BlockSpan
packages.description: Expand a byte request to whole storage blocks.
packages.contract: Returns [aligned start, bytes to read, requested start within read]. A zero-length request incurs zero reads. Counts must remain exactly representable. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: blockspan_align(offset, length, block)
Returns [aligned start, bytes to read, requested start within read]. A zero-length request incurs zero reads. Counts must remain exactly representable.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin fitting a short byte request inside whole storage blocks.

packages.name: blyx-coalesceio
packages.title: CoalesceIO
packages.description: Count merged reads and extra gap bytes for sorted byte requests.
packages.contract: Returns [merged reads, fetched bytes, extra bytes spanning gaps]. Overlapping bytes are counted once. Positive request lengths are required. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: coalesceio_plan(starts, lengths, gap)
Returns [merged reads, fetched bytes, extra bytes spanning gaps]. Overlapping bytes are counted once. Positive request lengths are required.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin joining nearby reads across a small gap.

packages.name: blyx-pelican
packages.title: Pelican
packages.description: Compare per-request aligned I/O with coalesced unaligned reads for a sorted trace.
packages.contract: Returns [independent aligned bytes, coalesced read count, coalesced bytes, bridge-gap bytes]. Values describe two explicitly defined read strategies. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: pelican_reads(starts, lengths, gap, block)
Returns [independent aligned bytes, coalesced read count, coalesced bytes, bridge-gap bytes]. Values describe two explicitly defined read strategies.
packages.logoAlt: A brown pelican opens its ochre throat pouch beneath a long bill.

workflow.title: Compare merged reads with aligned per-request reads
workflow.description: The example's two merged ranges fetch ten bytes including a one-byte gap. Independent eight-byte-aligned reads would fetch 24.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-pelican.git
cd blyx-pelican
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "0,5,20" "4,3,2" 1 8
workflow.problem: Merging requests saves seeks but can read unused gap bytes. Report each cost explicitly before changing a storage access pattern.

packages.name: blyx-histquantile
packages.title: HistQuantile
packages.description: Locate a nearest-rank quantile in noncumulative histogram counts.
packages.contract: Returns [bucket index, one-based rank, total observations]. At probability zero select the first occupied bucket. Empty histograms are invalid. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: histquantile_bucket(counts, probability)
Returns [bucket index, one-based rank, total observations]. At probability zero select the first occupied bucket. Empty histograms are invalid.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin moving a percentile marker to the bucket that contains it.

packages.name: blyx-rankband
packages.title: RankBand
packages.description: Look up the finite interval represented by a histogram bin.
packages.contract: Edges must be strictly increasing. Returns [lower edge, upper edge, span]. Bins are half-open except the last, which may include its upper edge. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: rankband_interval(edges, index)
Edges must be strictly increasing. Returns [lower edge, upper edge, span]. Bins are half-open except the last, which may include its upper edge.
packages.logoAlt: Blyx penguin unfolding the two edge flags of a selected histogram bin.

packages.name: blyx-nightingale
packages.title: Nightingale
packages.description: Bound a percentile from histogram counts without inventing a within-bin value.
packages.contract: Returns [lower bound, upper bound, rank, classification]. Classification is -1 when the whole interval is below threshold, 1 when entirely at or above, and 0 when the bins cannot decide. The upper-bound comparison is deliberately conservative. Invalid arguments and nonfinite results return an empty vector.
api: nightingale_quantile(counts, edges, probability, threshold)

Returns [lower bound, upper bound, rank, classification]. Classification is -1 when the whole interval is below threshold, 1 when entirely at or above, and 0 when the bins cannot decide. The upper-bound comparison is deliberately conservative.
packages.logoAlt: A copper-tailed brown nightingale sings with its head held high.

workflow.title: Bound a percentile from histogram counts
workflow.description: The median is the fourth observation and lies in the 10–30 bucket. A threshold of 20 lies inside that bucket, so the classification stays unresolved.
workflow.command:
git clone --depth 1 --branch v0.1.0 https://github.com/Rahulchaube1/blyx-nightingale.git
cd blyx-nightingale
blyxc native-run project.blyx -- "2,6" "0,10,30" 0.5 20
workflow.problem: Histogram counts identify the bucket containing a percentile, not its exact location. Return the interval before deciding whether a threshold was breached.
